heading: Table State Persistence
text:
## Event Bus

The generated app wraps the page tree in an `EventBusProvider`. Custom components read it with `useEventBus()` (from `~/hooks`), which returns `{ publish, subscribe }`. It must run inside the provider, otherwise it throws.

- `publish(topic: string, ...args)` calls every handler registered for `topic`, synchronously, in registration order.
- `subscribe(topic: string, handler)` registers the handler and returns an unsubscribe function. Call it in a `useEffect` cleanup.
- Topics are plain strings. Generated pages use two formats, where `<pageXmiId>` is the page's XMI id from the UI model:
  - `refresh:<pageXmiId>` asks the page to reload its data. Operation actions publish it for the root page after they finish.
  - `<pageXmiId>:refreshed` is published with the fresh data after a page's refresh action succeeds.
- The XMI ids change with the model, so read them from the generated page file (the `<Page>XMIID` constant in `pages/types.ts`) instead of hard-coding them.

heading: Page Actions
text:
### `getMask`, `queryCustomizer` and template hooks

- **`getMask?: () => string`** is an optional member of the page actions hook for pages that show a view or a table, not for forms. A generated page calls it when it builds the `_mask` of its own load request, and falls back to a mask serialized at generation time. Return only the fields the page needs.
- **`_mask` syntax:** `{<attr>,<attr>,<relation>{<attr>,<attr>},...}`. The mask is wrapped in braces, plain attributes are comma separated and sorted, and a relation name is followed by its own braces. For example `{name,createdAt,owner{name}}`. Include every attribute that a visibility, enabled, required or range-bound field refers to, or the page cannot evaluate it.
- **`queryCustomizer`:** the page's refresh action takes a `QueryCustomizer` argument (`refreshAction?: (queryCustomizer) => Promise<JudoRestResponse<...>>`). It carries `_mask`, filters, sort and `_seek`. Overriding `refreshAction` replaces the load call, so pass the received `queryCustomizer` through (with your changes) to the generated service. Tables build it internally and add `_mask` from `getMask` when present.
- **`post<GetTemplateAction>(ownerData, data, storeDiff)`** exists only on dialog (create-form) hooks. It runs after the template (default values for a new instance) has loaded. Use `storeDiff(attributeName, value)` to write defaults into the form data. It is not generated on plain pages.

heading: Field Validation
text:
### Hook member names

- The handler for a required rule is `is<Field>Required`, with `<Field>` the attribute name with its first letter in upper case (`isNameRequired`). The generated types contain no `isFieldRequired`; `isFieldRequired` is a placeholder name only. The same pattern applies to `is<Field>Hidden`, `is<Field>Disabled` and `is<Field>Readonly`. The signature is `(data, editMode, isLoading...) => boolean`: take it from the generated `types.ts`.
- Range and refresh members of an actions hook are named `<relation><Kind>Action`, where `<relation>` is the relation name (omitted on a container's own table) and `<Kind>` is the action kind: `refreshAction`, `<relation>AutocompleteRangeAction`, `<relation>SelectorRangeAction`. A range override receives `(queryCustomizer)` and returns the target rows.
- Cards container configuration: see Extension Points, Cards Configuration Hook.

heading: Cards Configuration Hook
Container Hook Registration
text:
### Generated page files

Each page folder (`src/pages/<Page>/`) and dialog folder holds these files:

- `index.tsx`: the page component. It loads data, builds the page actions (merged with the custom hook if one is registered) and renders the container inside the view-model provider.
- `context.tsx`: declares `<Container>ViewModel` (the container's page props plus `setIsLoading`, `setEditMode`, `refresh`, and `selectionDiff` on selector pages), the `<Container>ViewModelContext` and the `use<Container>ViewModel()` hook. Child components and custom elements call that hook to reach page state and actions. It throws outside the provider.
- `customization.ts`: declares the actions hook contract: `<PAGE>_ACTIONS_HOOK_INTERFACE_KEY` and the type `<Container>ActionsHook = (data, editMode, storeDiff?, selectionDiff?, refresh?, submit?) => <Container>PageActionsExtended`.
- `types.ts`: declares `<Container>PageActionsExtended` (the container's action types plus the optional `post<Action>` handlers) and the `<Page>XMIID` constant.

`src/config/layout.ts` is app-wide: layout constants (`DRAWER_WIDTH`, `MINI_DRAWER_WIDTH`, `DIVIDER_HEIGHT`, `SUBMENU_MIN_WIDTH`), the `ThemeMode`, `MenuOrientation` and `ThemeDirection` enums, the customization prop types, `defaultLayoutConfig` (the menu orientation comes from the model, other defaults are fixed: light mode, header on, boxed container) and the `menuBehaviour` options. Do not edit it; it is regenerated.

heading: Available Fragment Extension Points
text:
Frontend (React) fragments, all placed in the override directory under `actor/`:

- `actor/package.json.dependencies.extra.fragment.hbs`, `actor/package.json.dev-dependencies.extra.fragment.hbs` and `actor/package.json.scripts.extra.fragment.hbs` add entries to the matching `package.json` section.
- `actor/public/i18n/application_default_extra.fragment.hbs` adds translation keys to the default language file. The stub is `"__extra": "Placeholder for additional translations",`, so write JSON key-value lines with a trailing comma.
- `actor/src/fragments/operations/operation-primary-output-handler.fragment.hbs` is included after each operation call, with `operation` and `action` in context. The stub is an empty comment. Use it to handle the operation result.
- Theme fragments are covered in [Theming](../frontend/theming.md).

In templates, `elementHasAnnotation(element, "<name>")` is true when the model element has an annotation with exactly that name, and `operation.output.target` is the output's target class type. To keep a literal Handlebars expression in the generated file, escape it with a backslash: `\{{name}}` renders as `{{name}}` (the generated i18n files use this for i18next placeholders).

heading: Platform base
text: The `@redirect` annotation is not read by the generator or the templates: no `redirect` string occurs in the Java helpers or the `.hbs` files. The only redirect mechanism in the generated app is `OperationFlowManager` (`handleResult`, `shouldUseCustomFlow`), already documented. Reword the note to say `@redirect` is a project convention that a custom `handleResult`/`shouldUseCustomFlow` reads, not a platform annotation.

heading: ID to data-testid Mapping
text:
Generated layout sections (`Flex` containers, accordions, cards and their grid wrappers) carry two attributes: `data-testid="<xmiId>"` and `data-name="<element name>"`. Select a section for CSS or tests with `[data-name="<Name>"]`; the name is the model element name, so it survives model id changes but must be unique per page to be unambiguous. The page header uses `data-name="PageHeaderContainer"`.

A container layout cannot be swapped by a runtime hook. Replace it either with a custom implementation element on the container's visual element, or by overriding the generator template `containers/widget-fragments/flex.hbs` through the generator override directory (same-name template override).

heading: Validation Errors Without Location
text: Validation errors (HTTP 400) are translated with the key `judo.error.validation-failed.<CODE>`, falling back to the message in the error. Example: `IDENTIFIER_ATTRIBUTE_UNIQUENESS_VIOLATION` ("Identifier attribute is not unique") is returned when a value is already used by another instance of an entity whose attribute is marked as identifier; its details carry `feature` (attribute name) and `value`. Override the text by adding that key to the app's i18n files.

`INVALID_CODE` and `getErrorCodeLiteralByOrdinal` do not occur in any judo-ng source, template, documentation or generated-code template. They are not platform names. Do not document them unless a project shows where they come from.

heading: Custom Component Data Access
text:
### Generated relation service methods

For a relation `<rel>` on class `<Class>` the generated service (`<Class>ServiceImpl`, from `~/services/data-api/rest`) has these methods, each present only when the relation allows it. `owner` must carry `__signedIdentifier`; `selected` items are serialized as references.

| Method | Present when | Signature |
|---|---|---|
| `getRangeFor<Rel>` | relation has a range | `(owner?, queryCustomizer?, headers?) => Promise<JudoRestResponse<Array<Target>>>`. Backs the range dialog and autocomplete. |
| `set<Rel>` | settable | `(owner, selected: Target \| Array<Target>) => Promise<JudoRestResponse<void>>`. Replaces the relation; collections take an array. |
| `unset<Rel>` | unsettable (optional single relation) | `(owner) => Promise<JudoRestResponse<void>>`. This is the "clear" for a single relation. |
| `add<Rel>` | collection, addable | `(owner, selected: Array<Target>) => Promise<JudoRestResponse<void>>` |
| `remove<Rel>` | collection, removable | `(owner, selected: Array<Target>) => Promise<JudoRestResponse<void>>` |

There is no `clear` method for a collection; call `set<Rel>(owner, [])` only if the relation is settable (verify on the generated service). Failures throw an `AxiosError` whose `data` is a `FeedbackItem` list (400, 401, 403).

heading: Widget Components
text:
- **Boolean combo:** the trinary-logic combo has three entries, `Yes` (true), `No` (false) and `Unknown` (null or undefined). The generated widget therefore shows "unknown" for an empty value.
- **Hide a row action per row:** set `hiddenBy` on the row button to a boolean attribute of the row's transfer object. The generated table hides the button when `!!row.<attribute>` is true. There is no other per-row hook.
- **Count only:** a table with `showTotalCount` sends the header `X-Judo-CountRecords: true` on its list call and reads the total from the `X-Judo-Count` response header. A count-only call is a list call with that header and `_mask: '{}'` (and a `_seek` limit of 1); read the header from the response, ignore the body.
- **Route parameters:** a page route is the page name split at `::`, each part capitalized and joined with `/`, plus `/:signedIdentifier` when the page is a view on a relation (or a refreshable output view), unless it opens in a dialog or is a single-access page. The identifier in the URL is the signed identifier (`__signedIdentifier`) of the row.

The old `/{model}/{actor}` context path is not found in the React template; routes are derived from the page name (see above). A count-only recipe is not generated anywhere; the `_seek` limit of 1 part is an inference and should be verified before documenting.

heading: 10. Operations wiring
text: **Operation output pages.** For an operation that returns a mapped transfer, the generated output page is a dialog with these actions: Back (always), Refresh (when the output transfer is mapped to an entity), Update (when that transfer declares `update`) and Delete (when it declares `delete`). The page type for the update action is `OPERATION_OUTPUT_UPDATE`; its action is named `<operation>::Update`. Unmapped outputs get only Back.

The output `behaviours` list and the order of generated input and output pages were not found in the transformation sources read; the output actions above come from the transfer's declared members instead.

heading: 10. Operations wiring
text: **`confirmationCondition`.** An operation button with a confirmation asks before it runs. Without `confirmationCondition` it always asks. With it, set to a boolean `DataMember` on the owner transfer object, the dialog appears only when that attribute is true in the current data (the row for table buttons, the owner data otherwise). The message comes from `confirmationMessage` and the translation key `<button key>.confirmation`.

`useJudoNavigation()` keeps a breadcrumb stack, not the browser history. `navigate(to)` pushes the current page onto the stack, `back()` pops it, `navigateBackTo(item)` truncates the stack to an item, `clearNavigate(to)` empties the stack and goes to `to`, and `externalNavigate(url)` sets `window.location`. `isBackDisabled` is true when the stack is empty, and `setTitle(title)` sets the label of the current page (a missing title logs a warning). With an empty stack, `back()` goes to the dashboard.

heading: IMaskInput Integration
text: The model attribute `textMask` is not read by the React generator: no generated widget applies it. The generated app only lists `react-imask` as a dependency. To get an input mask, register a custom implementation element for the field and use `IMaskInput` as shown here.

heading: Page Container Types
text: The UI model has no per-device (mobile, tablet, desktop) containers, and the generator does not read device-specific layouts. A section's width is its `col` value out of 12 (scaled by the parent's `col`), applied from the `md` breakpoint up; below `md` every section is full width (`xs: 12, sm: 12`). For device-specific rendering use a custom implementation element with MUI `useMediaQuery`.

The generated Auth gate renders the guest page (a login button unless replaced) whenever the user is unauthenticated and supportGuestAccess is true; no generated page or menu is reachable before sign-in. The template's openspec says the app 'renders without requiring authentication', which conflicts with Auth.tsx. Not settled: whether an anonymous actor gets its own working app.
